newsitem.title: USA: Tech decline picks up speed, pressures Nasdaq.
newsitem.headline: Tech decline picks up speed, pressures Nasdaq.

text.p: Nasdaq stocks suffered on Wednesday as the recent selloff in technology shares gained speed, traders said.

The Nasdaq composite index dropped 12.63 points or 0.96 percent to an unofficial close of 1304.13. Nasdaq shares have fallen in four of the five most recent sessions. The Dow industrials slipped about 46 points to close unofficially at 7039.

"The whole market was down. There's interest rate concerns, everyone's waiting to see what will happen next. Basically, there's really nothing to spark a great rally in techs when the market is this skittish," one trader said.
Cisco Systems Inc led the Nasdaq decline, falling 1-7/8 to 50-7/8 on heavy volume. Sun Microsystems Inc lost 2 to 29-3/4 and Intel Corp eased 1-1/8 to 142-3/4.
In other news, Access Health Inc dropped almost 32 percent, down 7-1/8 to 15-3/8, after the company said it expects fiscal 1997 to fall short of analysts' estimates.
Overall, declining issues beat gainers 2621 to 1744 on total volume of about 576 million shares.
